did: Built and tested live in the browser pane by hand. A shop (Karim Pharmacy) bought 612 taka of goods at the counter and paid 200 now; the memo was finished with the rest due. An older memo of 1,000 taka left on credit 45 days ago was added to the test data by a command. The owner then opened the new Credit ledger, Karim's account, and took a payment of 1,100 taka by bKash.

checks.text: The Credit ledger lists each customer who owes us, biggest first, with the total in large type (1,712 taka) and a count of customers who are late; Karim shows a Late mark with the text (45 days) and not only a colour
Memos left Due with no customer on them cannot be chased by name, so they are counted in a note instead (141,087 taka on 105 old test memos) with a link to All orders
Karim's account shows what he owes (1,412), a Take payment panel with the amount, an All-of-it shortcut, the way paid (cash, bKash, Nagad, Rocket, bank, card) and a note
A payment of 1,100 went to the oldest memo first: the 45-day-old memo was cleared and the newer one shows total 612, paid 300 (200 + 100), 312 still owed
Payments received lists each part with its memo, the way paid, who took it and the note; the customer's page in Customers now says Owes us 312 with a link to the account
A payment bigger than what is owed, a zero amount and an unknown way are all refused (automatic tests); it also works at 320 px wide and in dark mode, with no sideways scroll

notes: Built this round from the spec (chapter 28, note 12: the ledger is built separately and connected to the memo's Paid/Due mark). New tables invoice_payments and supplier_payments; services Receivables and Payables; the old Take payment on All orders now goes through the same service. The old memo was made by a command to show Late and the oldest-first rule. Not built: reminders to customers, interest, credit limits, and a customer's own view of what they owe. 20 new automatic tests.
